page: Amazon Web Services m8ine.xlarge is an eighth-generation general purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores clocked at 3.9 GHz, supported by 480 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is set at 16.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no local instance storage and relies on network-attached storage, with baseline network bandwidth rated at 6 Gbps. Hardware acceleration features include Intel AMX (amx_tile, amx_int8) and AVX-512 vector extensions.

Benchmark data reflects exceptional single-threaded performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2269.0 placing it in the top tier of evaluated hardware. Single-threaded data handling is robust, reaching 34.4 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.56 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, aggregate multi-threaded capabilities are limited by the physical 2-core budget; multi-threaded stress-ng throughput sits in the lower quartile, and Geekbench multi-core performance is moderate at 5202.0. Similarly, memory bandwidth reaches 46.95 GB/sec for uncached read-only blocks, and database operations in PassMark register in the bottom quartile.

Without integrated local NVMe storage and with hardware resources limited to 4 vCPUs, the m8ine.xlarge is balanced for workloads emphasizing single-thread execution speed, instruction set acceleration, or medium memory footprint over raw parallel throughput. Cost efficiency is driven by its modern Intel Xeon architecture and DDR5 speeds, though instances requiring extensive thread parallelism or fast local disk I/O may require larger tier configurations. Suitable workloads include web serving, API gateways, CI/CD compilation, and lightweight caching layers like Redis.
description: Amazon Web Services m8ine.xlarge is a Nitro-based general purpose instance featuring a 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores. It provides 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, delivering a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, alongside 6 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and no local storage. Hardware-level acceleration includes AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix instructions. Benchmark results highlight top-tier single-core performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2269.0 and fast compression throughput. However, its multi-core capabilities remain modest due to the 2-core physical limit, yielding average Geekbench multi-core scores and lower-quartile stress-ng results. Given its strong per-core frequency, DDR5 throughput, and standard memory density, the instance is well suited for web serving, microservices, software builds, and lightweight application runtimes requiring high single-thread efficiency.
